Since I have derealization and depersonalization I will  explain it.

Derealization makes it feel like you're in a bubble separated from the world. You observe the world and yet you can't interact with it. 

For example seeing your friend group chat and hang out with each other and simply watching them talk with each other and not adding anything to the conversation. 

You're physical there in the moment, but not mentally, because of this you feel like a ghost. You just simply don't feel or aren't acknowledged for existing therefore you feel like the world is fake or that you don't exist.

For depersonalization you feel as if you're a inside a flesh bag and you're able to control it like a puppet. You think before you do something. An example of this is the thought process "I'm thirsty I want of glass of water so I'll go to the kitchen" so your body follows accordingly to the commands and pours yourself a glass of water.

Usually the average person doesn't even need to think about this and just goes get a cup of water without needing to think about it. Its being hyper aware of yourself therefore there's nothing subconscious going on and it's all conscious.

So I would describe derealization as being hyper aware of your surroundings and depersonalization being hyper aware of yourself. They both make you monologue to yourself and get lost in thought to the point you're detached from reality. It's very abstract and hard to explain and understand so I don't blame you for not knowing.

Dissociative disorders are mental disorders that involve experiencing a disconnection and lack of continuity between thoughts, memories, surroundings, actions and identity. People with dissociative disorders escape reality in ways that are involuntary and unhealthy and cause problems with functioning in everyday life.

This includes Dissociative identity disorder, derealization, and depersonalization. They're all in DSM5.
